question: Názov švajčiarskej firmy Victorinox, ktorá vyrába známe červené vreckové nože, spája meno zakladateľovej mamy Viktórie a skratku jedného materiálu. Akého?
source_excerpt: The combination of the two words "Inox" and "Victoria" results in today's company and brand name – Victorinox.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone knows the red Swiss Army knife, but few notice that its maker's name hides a dedication to a mother and a word for a material. Slovaks know 'inox' and 'nerez' from kitchen sinks and pots, so they can work it out.
extra.verification_notes: Victorinox = Victoria (Elsener's mother) + inox (stainless steel, from French inoxydable), per the company's history page https://www.victorinox.com/en-CH/All-about-Victorinox/History/cms/history/

explanation: „Inox“ pochádza z francúzskeho slova inoxydable, teda nehrdzavejúci, a rovnaký nápis nájdete aj na nerezových drezoch a hrncoch. Zakladateľ Karl Elsener tak v jednom slove uctil mamu aj materiál, ktorý jeho nože preslávil.

question: Legendárny vreckový nožík, ktorý v Československu nosil vo vrecku takmer každý chlapec, dostal meno podľa tvaru svojej rúčky. Ako sa volá?
source_excerpt: Rybička (English: Little Fish) is a small Czech pocket knife with the handle shaped as a fish.

extra.why_interesting: Almost every Slovak adult held one as a child but never thought about the name. The stem says the name comes from the handle's shape, so the player can picture the knife and work it out. The payoff is the realization that it is still made today.
extra.verification_notes: Rybička is the Mikov pocket knife with a fish-shaped handle, popular across Czechoslovakia (also made by Sandrik in Slovakia), per https://handwiki.org/wiki/Engineering:Rybi%C4%8Dka_(knife).

explanation: Kovová rúčka má tvar rybky aj so šupinami a oškou. Firma Mikov ju v českých Mikulášoviciach vyrába dodnes, takmer v nezmenenej podobe.
